core_insight.source_excerpt: narma is an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" designed for AI-first companies to see, prove, and deploy AI automation at scale. The architecture has three layers. Observe (Layer 1): lightweight desktop sensors capture work patterns including application usage, activity sequences, and time allocation. Intelligence Layer (Layer 2): a "Brain" that detects employee intent, the business value of tasks, and "drift" where work diverges from the intended flow. Execution Layer (Layer 3): an "Agent Factory" that automatically generates, deploys, and monitors AI agents for validated high-ROI opportunities with built-in approval gates.
core_insight.if_wrong: If narma cannot accurately observe work patterns, detect intent, or identify drift, or if its agent factory fails to generate effective AI agents, then AI-first companies will not achieve the promised ROI and continuous AI uplift, undermining the venture's value proposition.
core_insight.why_different: narma differentiates itself by focusing on a comprehensive, three-layered architecture (Observe, Intelligence, Execution) that leverages existing foundation models to understand the 'Work Graph' and continuously deploy AI agents, rather than building proprietary LLMs.

market_data.why_better: narma offers a single system to observe how work happens, decide what AI should do, and auto-build agents continuously, ensuring 'Continuous AI lift' and addressing the current struggles with telemetry, ROI, and drift. This suggests it is a more integrated and automated solution than alternatives.
market_data.trigger_now: Enterprises struggle with a lack of telemetry to pinpoint AI savings, unreliable ROI measurements, and constant drift in systems and human resources, creating an urgent need for a solution.
market_data.segment: AI-first companies seeking to deploy AI automation at scale.
market_data.alternatives: Current challenges include a lack of telemetry for AI savings, unreliable ROI measurements, and constant drift in systems and human resources, implying manual or ineffective tracking and deployment methods.

raw.thesis: narma is developing an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" for AI-first companies to address the challenges of deploying AI automation at scale. The core innovation lies in its three-layered architecture: an "Observe" layer with desktop sensors to capture work patterns, an "Intelligence Layer" that detects employee intent and business value of tasks while identifying workflow "drift," and an "Execution Layer" (Agent Factory) that automates the generation, deployment, and monitoring of AI agents. This system leverages existing foundation models, focusing on understanding the "Work Graph" to pinpoint inefficiencies and opportunities for AI intervention. narma aims to provide a continuous AI uplift by observing work, deciding AI actions, and continuously building agents. This venture is positioned to replace or significantly augment existing methods of identifying and implementing AI automation within large organizations, particularly those already leaning into AI-first strategies. The founder's goal appears to be building a growth startup, given the focus on enterprise-scale AI automation and continuous improvement. The venture is currently at the idea stage, with the description outlining the planned architecture and vision rather than implemented features or traction.
